There seems to be some wierdness with these five cards.  I don't think some of the conclusions being drawn are accurrate.

First, we know that the requirement to keep the card in play is the action is not the act of dealing damage of a specified amount.

0 was the worst/best concept to ever be added to mathmatics and numbers in general. posts.name: dypaca
posts.cooked:
The key to understanding these two cases is the order of resolving effects.  1) If resolving one effect triggers a second effect, resolve that second effect before completing the first.  2) If two effects are triggered by the same thing, resolve them in the order they entered play. 

So in the first case (ruling 5):

  1. Something causes the target to deal damage, triggering the redirection effect (the middle paragraph of wrest the mind)
  2. The damage is redirected, then Visionary deals it 3 damage, destroying it and triggering the destruction effect (the final paragraph of wrest the mind)
  3. Wrest the Mind is destroyed and leaves play.

After resolving step 3 you would normally go back up to finish the second effect and Visionary would damage herself, but the card and effect are now gone.  So now you go back up to the first effect, which is also gone.  (Unless the effect causing the target to deal damage was not on the target itself, in which case you now continue resolving it)

In the second case (ruling 17):

  1. Something destroys Sonic Mine, triggering both the Sonic Mine to deal damage and Wrest the Mind to destroy itself (They each resolve in the order they entered play)
  2. Resolve Sonic Mine dealing damage, each one triggering the redirection effect on Wrest the Mind.  (for each damage she chooses to redirect, Visionary deals the Mine and herself damage, but the mine can't be destroyed again so this does not trigger the third paragraph of Wrest the Mind)
  3. Resolve the third paragraph of Wrest the Mind, now taking its turn to react to the destruction in step 1.  Wrest the Mind is destroyed and leaves play.

Now there was some debate on whether order of play should really be the key here or if "When this card is destroyed" effects should always take precedence.  In the case of Wrest the Mind though, it necessarily entered play after the target it is next to anyway, so that question only matters for other chain reactions like Ammo Drop + Tome of the Unknowable.

Wrest the Mind carries on with a "If you do" clause, so that interrupts Hammer's damage and proceeds with Wrest the Mind. Now Visionary will deal Hammer and herself 3 psychic damage. It goes in order of the card, so Hammer will take the damage first. Hammer recieves his 3 psychic damage, thus causes him to be reduced to 0. Since Hammer is now at 0 HP, he is effectively destroyed and is leaving play. Oh look, Wrest the Mind has a trigger for if the target it is attached to leaves play, thus interrupting the section of Wrest the Mind we were already on. When the target leaves play, Wrest the Mind is destroyed. Now that is taken care of, we can return to the other part of Wrest the Mind, oh look it's no longer in play, so its text is no longer valid. Meaning we can go back to Hammer, oh wait, he is gone aswell, no longer important. The game will than carry on as normal.

Now lets say Wrest the Mind is on Sonic Mine. Good ol' Mr. Fixer decides to use Strike for 1 point of melee damage to the Sonic Mine, reducing it to 0. Now it will be destroyed, but it has a destroyed trigger, so before it leaves play it will carry out this trigger. It will deal all hero targets the 2 sonic damage, Visionary will decide to redirect the first one to Ambuscade. So the next part of Wrest the Mind kicks in again, dealing the Sonic Mine and herself 3 psychic damage. First off the Sonic Mine takes the damage, being reduced to -3 HP, something would usually be destroyed at this point, but it is already in the process of it, so nothing happens for that. Then Visionary will take her 3 psychic damage.  She chooses to do the same thing for the second instance of damage, which will lead to the same result, 2 to Ambuscade, 3 to the Sonic Mine which will be at -6, and 3 more to Visionary. After Sonic Mine is done doing damage, it will leave play, finally destroying Wrest the Mind with it.

 

In all honesty though, if you are in that situation, you might as well target Visionary for the first instance of Sonic Damage, allowing her to be hit and can no longer deal damage because of it, then redirect as normal without Visionary doing anything else damage.
